evidence.summary: New theory-only method: inspect the negative-space rhythm of the whole Chinese wordmark and its adjacent glyph pairs before changing contours; equal glyph-box spacing is not the same as optical balance.
evidence.detail:
Date: 2026-11-19. Root cause/question: We have repeatedly judged contours and individual glyphs in isolation; could a mark still feel mechanically assembled because the spaces between strokes, within glyphs, and between neighboring glyphs form inconsistent white rhythms? This is distinct from the prior instrument/gesture-first research: this test holds the lettering shape fixed and diagnoses the space it creates.
Source #1, full article read: justfont, 蘇煒翔, "字型下載之前，先看看字型是怎麼製作的", 2015-07-14, https://blog.justfont.com/2015/07/check-this-out-b4-downloading-fonts/ . Relevant complete article sections: initial Chinese font design, framework/skeleton, spacing distribution, representative-character tests, visual fatigue, peer review and print/size checks. Key finding: Chinese glyph quality cannot be judged from a single character; mixed strings reveal inconsistent scale, center of gravity and spacing; designers test characters in rows, revise, print at different sizes and cross-review. Full article text read.
Source #2, full manual section read: FontLab 9 "Designing the Whitespace", accessed 2026-11-19, https://help.fontlab.com/fontlab/9/articles/designing-the-whitespace/index.html . Key finding: form and counterform must be judged together; white areas within and between glyphs create rhythm; identical numeric sidebearings do not guarantee identical perceived gaps. This manual's examples/metrics are primarily glyph spacing, so the concept transfers but numerical values do not.
Source #3, full article read: Adobe, "An introduction to kerning", accessed 2026-11-19, https://www.adobe.com/creativecloud/design/discover/kerning.html . Key finding: optical space is subjective and pair-specific; inspect at relevant sizes, isolate problem pairs but return to whole word, get external eyes, step away and print. Its examples are Latin; only the shape-based spacing concept transfers to Chinese, not Latin pair values.
Source #4, official Illustrator spacing/kerning reference, https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/design-with-text/edit-format-text/adjust-line-and-character-spacing.html ; relevant section was retrieved (optical, metrics and manual kerning/tracking); full 1,649-line navigation/content page not read, so not claiming full page read.
New operational tactic/hypothesis: do not immediately edit glyphs. On a frozen wordmark, make a spacing audit sheet with ① whole-word black/white silhouette at actual target size and thumbnail ② internal white pockets (中宫/笔画间白) ③ each adjacent-character gap as a pair, checking shape-based area/width and perceived rhythm, not forcing equal numeric gaps ④ compare horizontal flip and distant-view checks only as diagnostic ⑤ make spacing-only corrections on a duplicate before any contour edit. Chinese characters are usually full-width square units, unlike proportional Latin, so this is an optical audit of custom marks, not a blanket kerning rule.
Minimal A/B experiment: same frozen glyph contours, same content, size, reference and time budget; A = existing spacing; B = spacing-only optical corrections from pair-gap/negative-space audit; do not rerender baseline or alter strokes; compare blinded at thumbnail and actual application size for word cohesion, readability, perceived balance and reference fit. A result requires the user's judgment.
Status: RESEARCH_ONLY; no small sample executed, no image/vector files changed, no pixels or Figma readback, no user acceptance. No skill/master rule promoted. Preserve prior gesture-first research and human-stopped attempts; this is a separate candidate tactic, not permission to reopen stopped work.
